newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus oil output seen slipping slightly in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Belarus oil output seen slipping slightly in 1996.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Belarus expects to recover 1.86 million tonnes (about 37,200 barrels per day) of oil in 1996, compared to 1.93 million tonnes (38,600 bpd) last year, an official at state oil concern Belnefteprodukt said on Monday.
"The total amount of oil recovered is dropping every year because of inadequate financing from the state budget," company Vice-President Vladimir Prokopchuk said, citing the figures.
"If the kind of financing that we have today continues, the output will drop by at least one percent every year."
Belarus requires 10-12 million tonnes of crude oil a year for domestic needs. Its two oil refineries yearly process 26 million tonnes of oil, most of it imported from Russia.
